description: w16a slot1 - w16b_cellweight: blend159av_h3 + w15f's c_avg correction with the additive weight fitted PER GENERATOR RULE CELL instead of globally. Cross-fitted CV 0.9700554 on the frozen SKF5 seed42 folds - the best CV number this workspace holds (prev best 0.9700528, w15f_antistudent_avg). PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION 0.97107, with 0.97108 the alternative: w15f's global-weight version of this same object sits at CV 0.9700528 / LB 0.97107, this file is +2.6e-6 of CV above it, and the within-family CV->LB slope is +1.77, so the predicted move is +4.6e-6 - under one grid step. THE FINDING, which inverts this workspace's standing instruction. c_avg is the only object built here all week that beats its own matched control on the labelled rows, and nobody had asked where it lives. Cut on the generator's seven rule cells with a within-bin permutation control re-binned INSIDE each segment (rank-based, so scale-free across segments), it is strongly non-uniform: chi2 52.21 on 7 df. Cell A (social>4) cond AUC 0.589702 vs ctrl 0.500498, z +5.16; cell B z +4.42; band z +3.50; but cell D z +0.32 and both-missing z +0.10. Same story on the mask: 0-missing z +4.91, 3+ missing z +0.15. w14d had located the AUC DEFICIT in cell D (13.5% within-cell plus the four largest cross-cell terms) and in the coin-flip band. So the one correction that works is worth essentially nothing where the pack is worst and everything where the pack is already strongest (cell A within-cell AUC 0.9845). Fix-it-where-it-is-worst is backwards here, and that is why every regional idea tried in this workspace - per-cell isotonic, cell-local boosting, iso_regime, resid_boost2 - read null: they were all aimed at D and the band. THE DECISION TEST. Coordinate ascent, 2 passes, grid 0..0.02 step 5e-4, weights searched on four folds and scored on the fifth. Global 1 weight +3.338e-6; A-only 2 weights +5.031e-6; per-cell 7 weights +6.195e-6; all 4/5 folds. Against SIZE-MATCHED PERMUTED-MEMBERSHIP controls: splitting one weight into seven at random COSTS 0.97e-6 and into two costs 0.26e-6, so the real segmentation pays back the selection toll and clears it by +3.825e-6 (7 params) and +1.953e-6 (2 params). Five independent per-fold ascents agree on the structure: G exactly 0.0000 in 5/5 folds, D 0.0000 in 4/5, A at 6-9x the global weight in 5/5. That ordering reproduces the cond-AUC column measured by a different instrument. Scale confound ruled out - c_avg is unit-sd within FOLD not within cell, and cell A's sd is 0.724 vs 1.000 global, which would explain a 1.4x weight ratio, not 6-9x. Honest caveat: the arm was chosen by a rule fixed in the script docstring before the run, but it is still a choice among cross-fitted candidates, so read this as +5e-6 over base against a matched-control floor of +2.4e-6 rather than +6.2e-6. NOT a deadline pick - 7 fitted parameters above the stack, where blend159av_h3 and blend160origm_h3 fit zero. Nothing here was chosen with reference to the public slice.

w15f — blend159av_h3 (CV 0.9700492) + the transductive teacher-minus-student residual REBUILT INDUCTIVELY on our own frozen SKF5 seed42 folds, weight cross-fitted inside the folds. Cross-fitted CV 0.9700528, the best CV number held in this workspace (prev 0.9700493). w15e could not score this mechanism because the author's artefact exists only on the 296,302 test rows; this run built it: 25 LightGBM teacher fits (4 inner x 5 outer + 5 outer), teacher held-out AUC 0.966840, then a smoother student regressing the teacher's percentile ranks while carrying the held-out rows at weight 0.5. Teacher reconstruction verified against his published test_teacher at rank corr +0.99529. FOUR RESULTS. (1) The correction is real but small: conditional AUC given the base 0.505819 vs a within-bin permutation control 0.500227+-0.00116 (z +4.84), cross-fitted dAUC +3.58e-6, 4/5 folds, and REAL-minus-matched-permuted-control +7.32e-6 (z +4.46) at the fitted weight. Above the 2e-6 reproducibility floor, ~1/50th of the 18e-5 gap to MILANFX. (2) THE TRANSDUCTIVE PART IS WORTH NOTHING: an identical student fitted WITHOUT the unlabeled rows gives a residual correlated +0.967 with the transductive one, and the pure difference has conditional AUC 0.500579 vs control (z +0.52). So it is an ordinary inductive function of the 12 columns and sits inside w15b's power bound, not a new signal class. (3) HIS 60/60 AND OUR RESULT ARE BOTH RIGHT - it is base strength. Same correction, same instrument, across bases: 0.969641 -> +1.62e-5, 0.969678 -> +1.60e-5, 0.969961 -> -3.2e-6, 0.970028 -> -7.2e-6, 0.970049 -> -3.3e-6. His anchors sit at 0.9697 where we measure +1.6e-5 against his reported +1.8e-5. The information is already inside our pack. (4) The student is the one hyperparameter he never published, so it is averaged out over three fitted across sd 0.048/0.031/0.020 bracketing his 0.0196, not hand-picked - the two fidelity criteria disagree (scale picks rough, shape picks mid). Nothing fitted against any leaderboard. Predicting 0.97105: h3-family invariance is 6/6 and this perturbation is spearman 0.9999928 to base, 4x smaller than w15e's file that moved one unit. NOT a deadline pick - one fitted parameter above the stack where blend159av_h3/blend160origm_h3 have zero.

w15i — blend159 (ens4, cross-fitted CV 0.9700434, unsent), sent to test a PRE-REGISTERED prediction and to dilute the auto-selection default. PREDICTION: 0.97106. THE CV->LB REGRESSION IS NOT DEAD; IT WAS FITTED WITH AN OMITTED VARIABLE. w14a pooled 34 readings across transform families and got slope +0.15/+0.22, R^2 0.03-0.08, and concluded CV had stopped predicting LB. But the same run measured a per-family residual offset spanning 51e-6, i.e. 7x the CV spread of the top pack - pooling that into a regression whose regressor spans 1e-5 destroys the within-group slope. Refitted with transform-family fixed effects on all 34 triples (CV recomputed from the stored OOF, LB read live): slope +1.77 +/- 0.24, t=+7.33, within-R^2 0.674, residual sd 5.8e-6 = 0.58 LB grid steps, against the pooled 19.3e-6. Assumption-free version: of the 32 within-family pairs the 1e-5 grid can resolve at all, 30 are concordant (93.8%, binomial p 1.2e-7). So the public LB is a SHARP instrument, resolution ~5.6e-6 in CV units (= one grid step / 1.77); the 11 h3/w files all landing on exactly 0.97105 is their 3.3e-6 CV span falling under that threshold, not the slice failing to resolve. Today's blend160origm (CV 0.9700442, sent 12:48 by another run) returned 0.97106 against the ens4-family fit's 0.971061 - one free out-of-sample confirmation already. blend159 is the second: CV 0.9700434 -> 0.971059 -> 0.97106. If it lands there it also enlarges the best-public tie from 3-good-of-4 to 5-good-of-6, cutting the auto-selection's limit-1 expected cost 35.5e-6 -> 26.7e-6. That is a dilution of an existing risk using a file CV already endorses, NOT a file built for the slice - and it is not a substitute for the click.

w15j — blend160origm, cross-fitted CV 0.9700442 on the frozen SKF5 seed42 folds: the highest-CV file this account has never sent (every file above it is already scored). 160-member ens4 stack, rank-average of all four transform stacks, whose 160th member is orig_binm. Closing agent for the day; sent on CV merit, nothing about it was chosen with reference to the public slice. PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION 0.97106: the ens4 CV->LB ladder is 3/3 at 0.97106 for CV>=0.970042 (blend159av/blend158/blend156) and 3/3 at 0.97104 for CV<=0.970034 (blend153/blend150sx/blend150fx); this file sits at 0.9700442, above the step. THE DAY'S CONSOLIDATED FINDING: the 18e-5 gap to MILANFX is mis-priced by the 5e-5 within-pack noise floor. w15a measured the CROSS-TEAM paired slice sd at 53-84e-6, making the gap 2.2-3.4 sigma and the four teams between 0.97113 and 0.97117 only 0.8-1.7 sigma. I validated that law against LIVE leaderboard data rather than simulation: over 112 CV-matched pairs of our own 36 scored files, spearman(1-rho, |dLB|) = +0.733 (p=4e-20), and pushing the law through the 1e-5 quantiser predicts the observed mean |dLB| at ratio 1.13 and 0.90 in the two buckets where the LB can resolve anything at all - a zero-fitted-parameter prediction. At the high-rho endpoint the 10 top-cluster files (CV 0.970046-0.970049, pairwise rho>=0.99992) read exactly 0.97105 with sd 0, which is what the law requires since it predicts sd(gap) 4.8e-6 under a 1e-5 grid. Also: the standing auto-selection risk is bounded at -10e-6, not -111e-6. blend158_logit is selected uniquely under NONE of six enumerated tiebreak rules at either selection limit, because it is neither earliest nor latest, neither lowest nor highest ref, and neither first nor last alphabetically in a 4-way tie whose other three members are all CV-good ens4 files. Deadline picks unchanged: blend159av_h3 + blend160origm_h3.

w15d — blend160orig_h3, cross-fitted CV 0.970046 on the frozen SKF5 seed42 folds, top cluster, never sent: the 160-member h3 stack (rank-average of hybrid/rankraw/rescale) whose 160th member is orig_bin, the LightGBM fitted only on the 7,500-row source dataset. Sent because this run's own work returned a null. THE ORIGINAL DATASET IS CLOSED FOR A NEW REASON. Positive ID: the deleted source algozee/smartphone-addiction-prediction-data is byte-identical to what we hold - the surviving notebook reads 'Smartphone_Usage_And_Addiction_Analysis_7500_Rows (1).csv' and danishzulfiqar5050's mirror carries that exact filename at md5 d831a326. The generator did far more than smear it. Two hard constraints, each in exactly one frame: competition satisfies daily>=social+gaming+work in 603,714/603,714 complete rows (original violates it in 60.7%), and the original satisfies weekend-daily in [0.50,3.00] in 100.0% of rows (competition only 52.0/52.1% train/test). Repairing the original's budget geometry - quantile-map its component/daily ratio onto the competition's, rescale the three components - lifts the original-trained transfer 0.885258 -> 0.921475, ten times the +36e-4 that missingness masking bought, at spearman 0.890 to the pack. It still contributes nothing: a perfectly-conditioned ONE-parameter rank blend on the frozen folds gives w*=0.002, in-sample gain +0.09e-6, cross-fitted -0.08e-6 (3/5). orig_binm gets w*=0.000 exactly against four packs, in-sample and cross-fitted, strictly less than a pure-noise control at w*=0.002. So the zero is the member, not the stacker's 1e18 condition number. Mechanism: the competition's addiction rate is monotone in social across its whole range (0.263/0.518/0.816/0.945/0.979/0.990/0.999/1.000) while the original's is flat 0.503-0.550 below social=4 and a hard 1.0 above. 86% of competition rows sit where the original teaches that social carries no signal. The two label functions differ on the majority of the frame, so the 7,500 rows have a low ceiling no extraction technique lifts.

w15b — blend159av_w, cross-fitted CV 0.9700482 on the frozen SKF5 seed42 folds: the best-CV file this workspace has never sent (only blend159av_wh3/_h3, blend160origm_h3 and blend158_h3 sit above it, and all four are already scored). Simplex-weighted combination of the four transform stacks over 159 members. Sent as-is because this was a measurement run that deliberately built no new model. What it measured instead: (1) the generator story in RESEARCH.md is a fact about the 7,500-row ORIGINAL, not about our frame — a full-lattice LightGBM on the two rule drivers scores 0.935111 on the 502,260 rows where both are observed, against the pack's 0.975431, so the other ten columns are worth +0.040319 and 'fit P(y|exact rule cell)' yields a FLOOR 40e-3 below us, not a ceiling; the nonparametric version is worse still (0.830 at 221k cells over 553k training rows, still climbing 66e-3 per doubling). (2) The within-column Bayes ceiling is not identifiable: there are ZERO duplicate rows on the 12-column vector, and for a calibrated field the Bayes AUC is identically the observed AUC — so no analysis of our own predictions can ever place a ceiling above us. Code control: in-sample isotonic gives A*-observed = -0.000000. (3) What IS identifiable is the PRICE. Solving for the family of truths consistent with our own measured AUC, the gap to MILANFX (18e-5) costs an ORTHOGONAL predictor of standalone AUC ~0.511, and the gap to LB rank 2 (11e-5) ~0.509 — stable to +-0.001 across calibrators spanning the whole dispersion sweep. That is a modest orthogonal nudge, not a new column. (4) The exact quantisation lattice is already absorbed: per-cell z-statistics give T/df 0.54 against a size-matched permuted control sitting at exactly 1.000, i.e. the pack tracks realised cell counts harder than binomial noise permits, while raw-feature members over-disperse 4.8-7.1x and single TE members 1.4-2.3x.

w15c — blend156w2, cross-fitted CV 0.970046 on the frozen SKF5 seed42 folds, never submitted by this account: 156 members under simplex weights over the four transform stacks, weights searched inside the folds. Exact 12-column feature twins between train and test: 2 of 296,302 test rows, and ZERO duplicate rows inside train's 691,369 — expected 0.005 pairs under column independence, since the effective lattice product is 4.5e16, so collisions were never arithmetically possible and the 'certainty' of them was a birthday-paradox error. WHAT IS THERE: train and test differ in per-column NaN rate at |z| up to 44 (daily 13.86->11.07%, social 19.38->16.00%, app_opens 11.67->8.68%) while per-row missing count matches (1.2589 vs 1.2729). It is decision-NEUTRAL: shift sd across 30 LB-scored files is 3e-6, corr -0.97 with CV, argmax unchanged (blend159av_h3 tops both criteria), LB-prediction residual sd identical at 2.4e-5, and it does not rescue blend158_logit.
